title: Regular -ar present
explanation: Remove -ar; add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an. Use the present for habits and current facts.

title: Regular -er present
explanation: Remove -er; add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -en. Notice nosotros ends in -emos.

title: Regular -ir present
explanation: Remove -ir; add -o, -es, -e, -imos, -en. Nosotros distinguishes -ir from -er.

title: Present e → ie
explanation: Change the last stem e to ie in stressed forms; nosotros keeps e. The endings follow the infinitive family.

title: Present o → ue
explanation: Change the last stem o to ue in stressed forms; nosotros keeps o. Costar commonly describes a thing, not a person.

title: Present e → i
explanation: These -ir verbs change the last stem e to i in stressed forms. Nosotros keeps e. Seguir also loses u before o.

title: Present irregular yo in -go
explanation: Memorize the yo form in -go. Tener and venir also change e to ie; decir changes e to i; oír has y in several other persons.

title: Present yo in -zco
explanation: These selected verbs use -zco in yo and regular present endings elsewhere. This is a teaching family, not a rule for every -cer or -cir verb.

title: Reflexive present
explanation: Match me, te, se, nos, se to the subject; put the pronoun before the conjugated verb. The infinitive ends in -se.

title: Plans: ir a + infinitive
explanation: Conjugate ir for the person, then add a and the unchanged infinitive. This construction describes plans or an approaching event.

title: Regular -ar preterite
explanation: Completed bounded events use -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron. Yo and él forms require written accents; nosotros matches present in spelling.

title: Regular -er / -ir preterite
explanation: Use -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron. This bank avoids vowel-stem and other irregular preterites.

title: Preterite spelling changes
explanation: In yo, -car becomes -qué, -gar becomes -gué, and -zar becomes -cé to preserve pronunciation. Other persons follow regular -ar endings.

title: Strong irregular preterite
explanation: Use the memorized irregular stem with -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, without written accents. Decir uses dijeron; hacer uses hizo.

title: Preterite -ir stem changes
explanation: These -ir verbs change e to i or o to u only in él / ella / usted and ellos / ellas / ustedes. Nosotros keeps the infinitive stem.

title: Past habits: -ar imperfect
explanation: Use -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban for background, ongoing situations and habitual past actions. Context separates yo from él.

title: Past habits: -er / -ir imperfect
explanation: Use -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían for background and repeated past actions. All these endings carry a written accent.

title: Future simple
explanation: Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the infinitive or listed irregular future stem. The future can predict and can express a guess.

title: Conditional simple
explanation: Add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the infinitive or irregular future stem. Use for hypothetical results and softened requests.

title: Present subjunctive
explanation: After a suitable trigger such as Espero que, use the present subjunctive. Start from yo present, remove o, and switch ar to e endings, er/ir to a endings; learn exceptions.

title: Imperfect subjunctive: -ra
explanation: Take the preterite ellos form, remove -ron, and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran; accent the nosotros stem vowel. Used after past wishes and in si hypotheses.

title: Affirmative tú commands
explanation: For regular affirmative tú commands use the él present form. Memorize di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven; this bank practices those eight plus two regular verbs.

title: Negative tú commands
explanation: Use no plus the tú present subjunctive. Affirmative and negative tú commands use different patterns. Any object pronoun goes before the verb.

title: Usted / ustedes commands
explanation: Use the usted or ustedes present subjunctive for formal commands. No creates a negative command with the same verb form. Both addressees are practiced.

title: Present progressive
explanation: Use estar plus -ando for -ar or -iendo for -er/-ir to emphasize an action in progress. Leer uses leyendo; dormir uses durmiendo; pedir uses pidiendo.

title: Present perfect
explanation: Use he, has, ha, hemos, han plus an invariant participle. Regular participles end in -ado or -ido; learn the listed irregular ones. Regional use versus the preterite varies.

title: Pluperfect: earlier past
explanation: Use había, habías, había, habíamos, habían plus an invariant participle for an action already completed before another past reference point.

title: Conditional perfect
explanation: Use habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían plus an invariant participle for a hypothetical completed action. A counterfactual si clause needs the appropriate past subjunctive.
